title: Return a structured, coded payload from 4xx/5xx Responses, never a bare string literal

facts.note: Test files are excluded by the source.

Code-level fact: changed non-test code contains a `Response` whose status is 4xx|5xx and whose body is a string literal, regardless of whether the body, the status, or neither was the edited part (e.g. a status changed from 200 to 500 on a literal body). Realized today by bun_security_hygiene_detector.
Detector finding from bun_security_hygiene_detector flagging `new Response("<literal>", { status: 4xx|5xx })`.

fires: Non-test Bun source contains `new Response("<string literal>", { status: 404 })` or any other 4xx/5xx status.
A change sets the status of a Response with a string-literal body from 200 to 500 (status-only change).
doesNotFire: A Response with a 2xx or 3xx status, whatever its body.
An error Response whose body is a variable or a rendered fragment.

given: Non-test Bun source contains a `Response` with a 4xx or 5xx status (an error_response)
when: that error Response's body is a bare string literal, whether the body or the status was the part written or changed
then: The error Response MUST carry a structured payload with an error code, not a bare string literal body.
prefer: Return a coded payload and render a user-facing fragment separately, e.g. `return Response.json({ error_code: "ORDER_NOT_FOUND" }, { status: 404 });`.
avoid: A bare string literal body on an error status, e.g. `return new Response("order not found", { status: 404 });`.
unless: The status is 2xx or 3xx (out of scope).
The body is a variable or a rendered fragment, which is not a bare literal.
The code is in a test file.
why: htmx swaps the response body into the live DOM, so a bare error string is not merely unstructured data a client must parse but markup rendered to the user verbatim, including whatever internal detail it carries (a stack frame, a table name, an upstream message); the structured payload is both the machine-readable contract and the boundary that stops internals leaking into the page. This is sharper in an htmx app than in a JSON API, which is why it is enforced rather than advised.
evidence: bun_security_hygiene_detector reports no ERROR-BARE-STRING-001 finding on changed non-test files.

Reviewer sees no changed non-test 4xx/5xx Response with a bare string literal body; where a literal body was replaced, it is a structured payload with an error code (e.g. `Response.json({ error_code: ... }, { status })`). Bodies that are variables or rendered fragments are not in scope.
verifier_detail: Detector pattern: flag `new Response("<literal>", { status: 4xx|5xx })` — first argument a string literal, status in 400–599.
error_response term: a `Response` carrying a 4xx or 5xx status; 2xx/3xx are ignored.
Do not flag when the body argument is a variable/identifier or a rendered fragment (non-literal expression).
rendered_verbatim term: what htmx does with a bare error string — swaps it into the live DOM, internal detail included; the structured payload is also the boundary that stops leakage.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Stack-neutral obligation RE-REALIZED for Bun: the python-pytest sibling matches FastAPI's `HTTPException(detail="...")`, which does not exist here — a Bun error IS a `Response` with a status.

sharedNodes.text: Strict disposition: the rule fails on every finding; it is enforced, not advisory.

additions.text: Language facts typescript/javascript for the Bun stack and the activation fact names/observability classification.
